claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
Untreated CoCrFeNi exhibits relatively high friction.
Untreated CoCrFeNi exhibits relatively high wear rates, especially when temperature and load vary.
Laser surface alloying can incorporate vanadium into the surface of CoCrFeNi.
Laser surface alloying with vanadium will produce an in situ vanadium-enriched surface layer.
The modified surface layer will contain predominantly V2O5.
The vanadium-oxide-rich surface layer will adopt a lamellar microstructure.
The proposed lamellar microstructure is conducive to self-lubrication.
Introduced vanadium will oxidize during or after laser processing.
Vanadium oxidation will form a protective oxide film with low shear strength.
The vanadium oxide film will provide a stable interfacial shear plane.
The stable shear plane will reduce interfacial friction.
The vanadium oxide film will reduce wear.
Vanadium-alloyed CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than untreated CoCrFeNi from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C in ambient air.
Vanadium-alloyed CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than untreated CoCrFeNi from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C in ambient air.
The lubricious oxide layer will remain effective under different applied loads.
The lubricious oxide layer will maintain its performance despite variations in environmental conditions.
Performance in extreme thermal cycling or highly aggressive environments has not been established.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome claims robustness to variations in environmental conditions, but the proposed testing is restricted to ambient air and the boundary states that performance in highly aggressive environments remains unverified.
